rationale: The compiled seed_edits, bindings, and selector now correctly realize the reviewed design. The ground-truth selector traverses user_teams→teams via team_id and applies role='owner' plus team_name='ClientOps Workspace' as a real, non-hidden identifying attribute pair, matching route_nodes (WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP, WORKSPACE) without merging the discovery-anchor channel into the formal identifying path — consistent with the design's intent that #clientops-main/#dataops-main serve only as actor-accessible discovery anchors (via conversations.info/members), not as part of the locked route. Mechanical checks show zero errors; computed_matches correctly isolates only Nora (U_NORA, T02CLIENTOPS, owner), and computed_focal_negatives/candidate_population correctly include Diego (admin, correct workspace), Felix (member, correct workspace), Zara (owner, wrong workspace), Ivy/Tom (wrong workspace and role), and all pre-existing Test Workspace members — giving the required role-vs-workspace contrast negatives. Actor (agent1) is granted membership and channel access in both anchor channels/workspaces, grounding the documented discovery path with no reliance on the disallowed workspace-name lookup capability. Answer_attributes are bare table.column names, resolution mode is single and correctly resolves to one unique match, and no unsupported API/write action is invoked (pure read task). Quality remains adequate: a plausible, well-motivated scenario with meaningful negatives, though it is a straightforward read/lookup rather than a consequential action.
